full_pass_recommendations.title: MOCK SOURCE ENVIRONMENT

criteria.finding: The opt-in coverage board exposes distinct requisitions A, B and C.
A retains two source posting IDs, distinct metadata and the same application route; the baseline A rows remain unchanged.
Annual ranges, an hourly B range, and explicit missing C salary/currency/period are asserted.
REMOTE, HYBRID, ONSITE and UNKNOWN remain explicit.
Each A/B/C board application URL redirects to its corresponding same-origin mock ATS path.
C exposes absent company and company_website without an invented identity.

caveats: This literal requirement is a local fixture environment. Successful production ingestion of an absent employer identity is not claimed. Opt-in coverage is deliberate; baseline behavior remains compatible.

full_pass_recommendations.title: MOCK COMPANY ENVIRONMENT

criteria.finding: The homepage and job records use the exact required fictional employer name.
The local /company homepage renders the named employer and careers link.
Real Chromium follows the Careers link from the homepage.
The /ats/example portal provides the Jobs navigation and provider/tenant identity.
The careers route redirects to /ats/example; HTTP and browser checks observe the redirect.
The portal exposes distinct A/B jobs. The actual fixture discover() pipeline runs twice and preserves two canonical jobs, four posting copies and one company source after database reopen.

caveats: Evidence is intentionally fictional and local; no public employer or external application submission is implied.

full_pass_recommendations.title: MOCK ATS ENVIRONMENT

criteria.finding: GET /ats/apply/A?flow=onepage renders one form whose complete successful submission is exercised by Chromium.
The default form advances through /ats/review and /ats/submit; real browser validation, review and confirmation are exercised.
A real fixture upload control accepts the synthetic PDF; absent, invalid and oversized uploads are rejected without a receipt.
The cover-letter control and shared server validation are exercised in the same complete forms.
Country and the active State or province controls are selected in Chromium.
The Remote role radio is asserted structurally and selected in the browser journey.
Document-review and explicit confirmation checkboxes are exercised, with required-field rejection before receipts.
The approved fictional answer is filled in both form variants; wrong answers are rejected by the server.
Country changes reveal/hide the dependent control, clear stale values and toggle required state; the active branch is separately server-validated.
Missing fields, wrong answers and invalid/oversized uploads return rejection without receipts; the browser displays a validation error before successful correction.
Both browser journeys reach the explicit confirmation screen. Durable receipt replay retains count=1 and rejects cross-job reuse.

caveats: This accepts the mock ATS environment, not all production application adapters. Direct one-page fixture/browser journeys do not prove that every adapter can drive that form.

The supported UI exposes scoring, source/route provenance and immutable document facts; current browser core/document history checks reran.

The remaining 21 active modules/32 injected dispatch sites now bound complete headers/body parsing; chained operations share finite budgets and mounted views release loading/cancel late effects. The evidence records 82 new direct deadline cases and 14 mounted lifecycle cases.

The six qualitative UX descriptors are assessed through the ten operational clauses in the literal specification, not as a claim that the whole product is complete.

Browser profiles remain fixed at output_dir/application_id/browser-profile, including manual auth.
Submission limits remain Policy() defaults; controlled dry-run pause/daily limits are API-only, per application and UTC day, and do not establish submission hourly/daily UI/environment configuration.

The test filename ending _276 is historical; this finding concerns MJ-REQ-275 and does not promote MJ-REQ-276.
